While knowing how to use Git on the command line remains essential
because it provides the full power,
flexibility,
and scriptability of Git,
graphical Git clients offer visual representations of repository history,
interactive branch visualization,
and simplified merge conflict resolution.

### GitHub Desktop {#sec-github-desktop}

[GitHub Desktop](https://desktop.github.com/) [@githubdesktop]
is a free,
open-source graphical interface developed by GitHub.
It simplifies basic Git workflows
such as staging changes,
creating commits,
branching,
and opening pull requests.
It is an accessible starting point
for beginners or for developers who prefer a visual interface
for routine Git operations.

### GitKraken {#sec-gitkraken}

[GitKraken](https://gitkraken.com/) [@gitkraken]
is a cross-platform (macOS, Windows, Linux) Git client
and developer experience platform.
Key features include:

- An interactive, visual commit graph that simplifies navigating complex branch histories
- Drag-and-drop interactive rebasing and visual branch merging
- An in-app merge conflict editor with side-by-side diffing
- Multi-repository workspaces for tracking and managing multiple repositories together
- Integrations with major Git hosting providers (GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, and Azure DevOps)
  and issue trackers such as Jira

Beyond the standalone GitKraken Desktop client,
the GitKraken ecosystem includes the GitLens extension for Visual Studio Code
and terminal CLI integrations.

### GitKraken Kepler {#sec-gitkraken-kepler}

[GitKraken Kepler](https://gitkraken.com/kepler) [@gitkraken-kepler]
is GitKraken's agentic development environment
and workspace intelligence platform.
It is designed to coordinate and manage agent-driven development workflows,
providing a unified interface to:

- Plan implementation work and orchestrate parallel AI coding agents at scale
- Generate context-aware commits, pull request summaries, and code reviews
- Inspect and review diffs and generated changes before shipping code
